entities.description: A spiritual leader of BAPS whose blessings are acknowledged in the publication.

entities.name: Mahapurushdas Swami
entities.description: One of Swamishri's sadhus who spoke on the greatness of a true sadhu during the festival at Sayajipura.

entities.name: Maharaj
entities.description: The central divine figure worshipped in the Swaminarayan Sampradaya, also referred to as Purushottam Narayan. He guided devotees, performed miracles, and established religious practices.

entities.name: Maharaja of Shirohi
entities.description: The ruler of Shirohi who was captivated by young Ladudanji's poetic recital and arranged for his further education.

entities.name: Maharaja of Shirohi
entities.description: The ruler of Shirohi who recognized Ladudanji's poetic talent and supported his further education.

entities.name: Mahashankarbhai Dave
entities.description: Father of Ganpatbhai, from Bharuch.

entities.name: Manjukeshanand Swami
entities.description: One of Maharaj's eight most famous poet-sadhus, mentioned alongside Devanand Swami.

entities.name: Merai devotee
entities.description: A devotee to whom Devanand Swami predicted his death and asked to make a wooden chair for carrying his body to the funeral pyre.

entities.name: Miyaji
entities.description: One of Maharaj's personal attendants whom Jhinabhai referenced as an example of those in eternal service to Maharaj.

entities.name: Mota Swami
entities.description: The affectionate name given to Sadhu Yagnapriyadas because he took initiation at the late age of 70.

entities.name: Motibhai
entities.description: A leading devotee who accompanied Swamishri and helped arrange money for the murtis.

entities.name: Motilal Fojdar
entities.description: A respected devotee in Mumbai to whom Nirgun Swami explained Shastriji Maharaj's greatness.

entities.name: Muktanand Swami
entities.description: A saint who had told Joban about Maharaj's greatness and who swung Maharaj on the hindolo during the Holi festival.

entities.name: Mulji Brahmachari
entities.description: One of Maharaj's personal attendants whom Jhinabhai referenced as an example of those in eternal service to Maharaj.

entities.name: Muljibhai
entities.description: A devotee through whose association Jethabhai came to understand Bhagatji Maharaj's greatness.

entities.name: Munibawa
entities.description: A profound scholar of Sanskrit and Vedanta philosophy who later became one of Maharaj's sadhus while keeping his original name.

entities.name: Nagar Brahmins
entities.description: A community that opposed the construction of the Junagadh mandir but later subsided their opposition.

entities.name: Naja Jogia
entities.description: A devotee who often spoke of Jhinabhai before Maharaj and wore a dhotiyu given by Jhinabhai in exchange for remembering him.

entities.name: Nar-Narayan Dev
entities.description: Divine murtis that were consecrated in the Ahmedabad mandir.

entities.name: Natvar
entities.description: A form of the divine mentioned in Brahmanand's couplet about devotional surrender.

entities.name: nawab
entities.description: The head administrator of Junagadh who was convinced by Brahmanand Swami of Maharaj's greatness and provided official backing for the mandir.

entities.name: Nawab
entities.description: The head of the royal court of Junagadh and the city's main administrator who respected Jhinabhai's devotion.

entities.name: Nilkanth Varni
entities.description: A form of Bhagwan Swaminarayan who visited Panchala along with Ramanand Swami when Jhinabhai was ten years old.

entities.name: Nirgun Swami
entities.description: A dedicated sadhu who helped Satsang grow in Mumbai through letters and visits. He was stern by nature but also forgiving, and wrote extensive letters to devotees in Africa.

entities.name: Nirgundas Swami
entities.description: One of three sadhus who spoke on the greatness of a true sadhu during the festival.

entities.name: Nirgundasji
entities.description: A swami of the Swaminarayan Sampradaya mentioned in the contents as one of the biographical subjects.

entities.name: Nishkulanand Swami
entities.description: A saint who built a beautiful 12-sided hindolo for Maharaj and set it up in Jnanbaug for the Holi festival.

entities.name: Nityanand Swami
entities.description: A sadhu who questioned Shuk Muni about his reaction when Maharaj tore up his night's work.

entities.name: Pandit Bhattacharya
entities.description: A renowned pandit in Dhamadka who taught Ladudanji Sanskrit and music.

entities.name: paramhansas
entities.description: A number of Bhagwan Swaminarayan's senior sadhus who were studying in Dabhan under a learned scholar and influenced Jagannath toward satsang.

entities.name: Parshads
entities.description: Category of devotees who formed one of the circles during the raas dance, positioned between sadhus and regular devotees.

entities.name: Pragji Bhagat
entities.description: A spiritual figure whom hostile sadhus could not speak against when Nirgun Swami was in Vartal.

entities.name: Prahlad
entities.description: A legendary devotee mentioned by Jhinabhai as an example of how divine care doesn't require parental requests when there is true devotion.

entities.name: Pramukh Swami Maharaj
entities.description: An important spiritual leader of BAPS, mentioned as the inspirer of the textbook series.

entities.name: Premanand Swami
entities.description: One of Maharaj's eight most famous poet-sadhus, mentioned alongside Devanand Swami.

entities.name: pujari
entities.description: The priest who came to perform mangala arti at 4 a.m. and found Yagnapurushdasji and Jethabhai talking.

entities.name: Purushottam Narayan
entities.description: Supreme form of God described as the cause of all avatars and manifest in human form.

entities.name: Radha-Raman Dev
entities.description: Divine murtis that were consecrated in the Junagadh mandir.

entities.name: Radharamanprasad
entities.description: Son of Acharya Lakshmiprasadji Maharaj whom Nirgun Swami was sent to bring from Chhapaiya.

entities.name: Raibai
entities.description: Jivuba's mother-in-law who understood her spiritual desires and helped convince her son.

entities.name: Raiji
entities.description: A devotee who confronted Joban Pagi when he tried to enter Bapujibhai's home at night.

entities.name: Ramanand Swami
entities.description: Sadguru who received both Ramanand Swami and Nilkanth Varni in his court in Panchala. He blessed Jhinabhai before passing away.

entities.name: Rameshbhai Dave
entities.description: Professor who assisted in the preparation of the Satsang Reader books.

entities.name: Ramji Keshav
entities.description: A respected devotee in Mumbai to whom Nirgun Swami explained Shastriji Maharaj's greatness.

entities.name: Ranchhoddas
entities.description: One of Bapujibhai's eight sons.

entities.name: Ranchhodray
entities.description: A deity at Dakor who granted darshan to Ashabhai in a dream and instructed him to take refuge in Bhagwan Swaminarayan.

entities.name: Rangbai
entities.description: Ranchhoddas's wife who served Maharaj with great love and arranged for his meals.

entities.name: Rantidev
entities.description: A legendary king who sacrificed everything in service of others, to whom Mota Swami was compared.

entities.name: Rao of Kutch
entities.description: The King of Kutch who hosted Ladudanji as a guest during his studies in Bhuj and tested his knowledge.

entities.name: Rao of Kutch
entities.description: The King of Kutch who hosted Ladudanji during his studies and later tested his knowledge in the royal court.

entities.name: Raya Khatan
entities.description: A devotee who quickly brought milk and thuli to serve Maharaj before he left Balol.

entities.name: Royal Goldsmith
entities.description: A goldsmith in the Bhavnagar court who wore distinctive tilak and chandlo marks, inspiring Ladudanji's inquiry about Swaminarayan.

entities.name: Sadguru Balmukunddasji
entities.description: A spiritual teacher whose discourses Jetha Bhagat listened to at Junagadh mandir.

entities.name: Sadguru Dharmaswarupdasji
entities.description: A spiritual teacher whose discourses Jetha Bhagat listened to at Junagadh mandir.

entities.name: Sadguru Jagatpavandas
entities.description: A spiritual teacher who would visit Pij from nearby Dabhan along with Shastri Yogeshwardas.

entities.name: Sadguru Krishnacharandasji
entities.description: A spiritual teacher whose discourses Jetha Bhagat listened to at Junagadh mandir.

entities.name: Sadguru Narayandasji
entities.description: A spiritual teacher whose discourses Jetha Bhagat listened to at Junagadh mandir.

entities.name: Sarasvati
entities.description: The goddess of learning who Bhagwan Shiv promised would reside in Devidan's heart.

entities.name: Shakaro Pagi
entities.description: One of Joban's three brothers.

entities.name: Shambhudanji
entities.description: The father of Ladudanji (Brahmanand Swami), who received divine inspiration through a dream.

entities.name: Shastri Yogeshwardas
entities.description: A spiritual teacher who would visit Pij from nearby Dabhan and helped Jethabhai grow closer to Satsang.

entities.name: Shastriji Maharaj
entities.description: A revered spiritual leader and guru who is described as having unmatched greatness. He is the one whose 80th birthday was celebrated in Bochasan.

entities.name: Shivji
entities.description: Hindu deity who appeared before Devidan and granted him darshan and a boon about Bhagwan Purushottam Narayan coming to his village.

entities.name: Shivshankarbhai
entities.description: A devotee who taught Jethabhai about Akshar-Purushottam upasana.

entities.name: Shri Krishna Bhagwan
entities.description: Hindu deity mentioned in comparison to Maharaj's divine power, specifically regarding lifting Mount Govardhan with one finger.

entities.name: Shriji Maharaj
entities.description: Another name for Bhagwan Swaminarayan, who came to Balol and initiated Devidan as a sadhu.

entities.name: Shrijiswarupdas
entities.description: One of Shastriji Maharaj's sadhus who traveled with Nirgun Swami to Kashi.

entities.name: Shuk Muni
entities.description: A great sadhu from Dabhan who was described by Maharaj as his right hand and was a Sanskrit scholar who wrote many religious texts.

entities.name: Shukanand Swami
entities.description: A Sadguru originally named Jagannath, born in 1799, who became a sadhu and served as Maharaj's secretary, known for his clear handwriting and devotion.

entities.name: Somla Khachar
entities.description: A devotee who acted as an intermediary, conveying Jagannath's request to Maharaj to become a sadhu.

entities.name: Sundar Pagi
entities.description: Joban's younger brother who refused to steal Maharaj's horse after having darshan.

entities.name: Sura Khachar
entities.description: Devotee who tried to cheer Maharaj along with others when he was disappointed with Jhinabhai's disobedience.

entities.name: Swami
entities.description: A divine figure mentioned alongside Maharaj who is pleased by the building of mandirs.

entities.name: Swami Jaga Bhagat
entities.description: One of Gunatitanand Swami's foremost disciples who resided in Junagadh and whose discourses Jetha Bhagat benefited from.

entities.name: Swami Nirgundasji
entities.description: A sadhu whose story begins in the text, originally known as Jethabhai of Pij.

entities.name: Swami Yagnapriyadasji
entities.description: A sadhu who is the subject of chapter 8, originally known as Ashabhai before taking vows.

entities.name: Swaminarayan
entities.description: The central deity of the Swaminarayan Sampradaya, also known as Bhagwan Swaminarayan and Shriji Maharaj.

entities.name: Swamishri
entities.description: A spiritual leader who accompanied Nirgun Swami on visits and was asked about what pleases Maharaj and Swami. He gave comfort to Nirgun Swami during his illness.

entities.name: Thakor Manubha
entities.description: Jhinabhai's father, a Solanki Vaghela Rajput and descendant of King Siddharaj Jaysinh, who was a disciple of Ramanand Swami.

entities.name: Thakorji
entities.description: The deity for whom golden sinhasans were constructed in Atladara mandir.

entities.name: Ullasrambhai
entities.description: A devotee who taught Jethabhai about Akshar-Purushottam upasana.

entities.name: Vasudev-Narayan
entities.description: A deity for whom arti was performed at Dada Khachar's darbar.

entities.name: Vignandas Swami
entities.description: One of Swamishri's sadhus who spoke on the greatness of a true sadhu during the festival at Sayajipura.

entities.name: Vishnu
entities.description: A major Hindu deity whose avatars were mentioned in Shuk Muni's letter comparing them to Maharaj.

entities.name: Yagnapriyadasji
entities.description: A swami whose story appears to be beginning at the end of the text, introduced as the subject of chapter 8.

entities.name: Yagnapurushdasji
entities.description: A spiritual leader studying in Rajkot whose fame spread widely within the Swaminarayan Sampradaya, later known as Shastriji Maharaj.

entities.name: Yogeshwardas
entities.description: A shastri who would visit Pij from nearby Dabhan and helped Jethabhai grow closer to Satsang.

entities.name: Yogiji Maharaj
entities.description: A saint known for his innate saintliness and humility. Nirgun Swami would bow before him and encourage others to recognize his true nature.

entities.name: Ahmedabad
entities.description: A city where Brahmanand Swami built a grand mandir and the location of the acharya who performed murti-pratishtha.

entities.name: Ahmedabad mandir
entities.description: The first mandir built by Maharaj, supervised by Brahmanand Swami, where Nar-Narayan Dev murtis were consecrated.

entities.name: Ajva Road
entities.description: A road near Vadodara where Swamishri advised devotees to purchase land when they decided to move from Sadhi.

entities.name: Akshar Ordi
entities.description: A sacred building where Maharaj appeared to Bhaguji after passing away and where spiritual conversations took place.

entities.name: Akshar-Purushottam mandirs
entities.description: Temples whose building pleases Maharaj and Swami, and devotees who offer seva towards building them are made brahmarup and taken to Akshardham.

entities.name: Akshardham
entities.description: The divine abode where devotees who serve in building mandirs are taken by Maharaj, and where Nirgun Swami took his place in eternal seva.

entities.name: Anand
entities.description: A place where Nirgun Swami was brought with Swamishri's permission during his final illness, where continuous prayers and discourses were conducted.

entities.name: assembly hall
entities.description: A building constructed by Mota Swami at Atladara mandir.

entities.name: Atladara
entities.description: A place where the Suvarna Mahotsav was held, during which Nirgun Swami's management skills shone through.

entities.name: Atladara mandir
entities.description: A temple where Mota Swami put finishing touches including assembly hall, dining hall, grand gate and golden sinhasans.

entities.name: Badrikashram
entities.description: One of the divine abodes offered by Maharaj to Jhinabhai as a destination after death.

entities.name: Balol
entities.description: A village near Dholka where Jijibhai lived and where Devidan was born on 9 November 1802.

entities.name: Bharuch
entities.description: The city where Mahashankarbhai Dave and his son Ganpatbhai lived.

entities.name: Bhavnagar
entities.description: The kingdom ruled by King Vakhatsinh where Ladudanji gave an exceptional performance and learned about Swaminarayan.

entities.name: Bhudej
entities.description: The village where devotee Khodabhai was from and where devotees went to inquire after Maharaj when he escaped from Vartal.

entities.name: Bhuj
entities.description: The city where Ladudanji studied Pingal Shastra and other poetic sciences for ten years under guru Abhaydanji.

entities.name: Bochasan
entities.description: A place where festival preparations were made and where Shastriji Maharaj's 80th birthday celebrations took place.

entities.name: Bochasan mandir
entities.description: A temple under construction in Bochasan that received financial support from Ashabhai and Ishwarbhai.

entities.name: Charotar
entities.description: A region in Gujarat where Shastriji Maharaj conducted his vicharan.

entities.name: Chhapaiya
entities.description: The place from where Nirgun Swami was sent to bring Radharamanprasad.

entities.name: Chhota Udepur
entities.description: A place where Ashabhai purchased farm lands to ease his financial difficulties, against Swamishri's advice.

entities.name: Dabhan
entities.description: The place of origin for Shuk Muni, a mango tree, and a bullock that Maharaj praised as being very useful to him.

entities.name: Dada Khachar's Darbar
entities.description: The assembly hall in Gadhada where Swaminarayan held gatherings with sadhus and devotees under a neem tree.

entities.name: Dakor
entities.description: A holy city where Ashabhai would go every Punam for darshan of Ranchhodray.

entities.name: Dhamadka
entities.description: A town in Kutch where Ladudanji learned Sanskrit and music from Pandit Bhattacharya and first met Ramanand Swami.

entities.name: Dharampur
entities.description: A place from which Maharaj was returning when he came to Vartal with Joban Pagi.

entities.name: dharmashala
entities.description: A rest house for sadhus that had been sanctified by Bhagwan Swaminarayan where Ashabhai first saw Shastriji Maharaj.

entities.name: Dhingda
entities.description: A village mentioned alongside Balol, on whose outskirts the Sankaleshwar Mahadev mandir is located.

entities.name: Dholka
entities.description: A place near which Balol is located, mentioned in connection with Devidan's birthplace.

entities.name: Dhrangadhra
entities.description: One of the states where Ladudanji performed and was received with great honor.

entities.name: dining hall
entities.description: A building constructed by Mota Swami at Atladara mandir.

entities.name: Dwarka
entities.description: One of the states where Ladudanji performed and was received with great honor.

entities.name: East Africa
entities.description: A region where Harmanbhai and Maganbhai established Satsang and where Nirgun Swami sent extensive letters to devotees.

entities.name: Gadhada
entities.description: The village where Maharaj held assemblies and where Jagannath went to meet him, featuring locations like the neem tree and Radha Vav.

entities.name: Gadhada mandir
entities.description: A temple whose arti Swamishri mentioned they still had to perform when encouraging Nirgun Swami during his illness.

entities.name: Golok
entities.description: One of the divine abodes offered by Maharaj to Jhinabhai as a destination after death.

entities.name: government depot
entities.description: A facility in Vadodara where Ishwarbhai had good contacts and could acquire festival supplies quickly.

entities.name: Gujarat
entities.description: The region where Joban and his brothers had made people tremble for years through banditry, and where they later served as Maharaj's bodyguards.

entities.name: India
entities.description: The country that was taken over by the British, affecting the religious practices of the Sampradaya.

entities.name: Jaipur
entities.description: A city from where murtis were required for Sarangpur mandir.

entities.name: Jamnagar
entities.description: One of the states where Ladudanji performed and was received with great honor.

entities.name: Jesangpura
entities.description: A place where Ashabhai purchased land with Swamishri's permission after deciding to move from Sadhi.

entities.name: Jetalpur
entities.description: A town near Balol where Bhagwan Swaminarayan completed a yagna before visiting Balol.

entities.name: Jnanbaug
entities.description: A location in Vartal where the 12-sided hindolo was set up for the Holi festival and where Rangotsav was celebrated.

entities.name: Joban Pagi's home
entities.description: Joban's house in Vartal where Maharaj stayed on the first floor during the Fuldol festival celebrations.

entities.name: Junagadh
entities.description: A city where Jhinabhai fell gravely ill and eventually passed away. Maharaj promised to build a mandir there for devotees of the Sorath region.

entities.name: Junagadh mandir
entities.description: A mandir built in Junagadh where Radha-Raman Dev murtis were consecrated and Gunatitanand Swami was appointed as mahant.

entities.name: Kala Bhavan Technical Institute
entities.description: The educational institute in Vadodara where Jethabhai came to study.

entities.name: Kariyani
entities.description: A place where Abhal Khachar first had darshan of Sahajanand Swami.

entities.name: Kashi
entities.description: A holy city where Nirgun Swami traveled after recovering from his injuries.

entities.name: Khan
entities.description: The village in the Shirohi region of present-day Rajasthan where Ladudanji was born on February 8, 1772.

entities.name: Khan
entities.description: The hometown of Ladudanji's uncle, where his family lived.

entities.name: Khandesh
entities.description: A region outside Gujarat where Nirgun Swami traveled annually to spread satsang among Gujarati immigrants.

entities.name: Khodiyar Mata mandir
entities.description: A temple dedicated to the goddess Khodiyar Mata that Maharaj visited and where he sprinkled gulal on the deity's murti.

entities.name: Koyli
entities.description: A place where another marvellous festival was held, inspired by Ashabhai and Ishwarbhai.

entities.name: Kundal
entities.description: Place where Amara Patgar and his son Hathiya Patgar lived.

entities.name: Kutch
entities.description: The region ruled by the Rao where Ladudanji stayed as a guest during his studies in Bhuj.

entities.name: Lakshmi Vadi
entities.description: A farm belonging to Dada Khachar and his family in Gadhada where Maharaj frequently visited and sat under a mango tree.

entities.name: Mahelav
entities.description: A place where Shuk Muni came after celebrating a festival in Vartal and gave vartman to Dungarbhai.

entities.name: Mahuva
entities.description: The destination where Jethabhai and Ganpatbhai safely reached by boat to have darshan of Bhagatji Maharaj.

entities.name: Mahuva mandir
entities.description: Temple in Mahuva where sadhus and brahmacharis resided and where Jethabhai would listen to discourses.

entities.name: mandir
entities.description: The temple where Jijibhai and Devidan went daily to worship Shivji.

entities.name: Mandirs
entities.description: Temples that Maharaj decided to build as part of his lasting legacy, following Muktanand Swami's advice.

entities.name: Mandvi
entities.description: A town in Kutch where Maharaj arranged a grand procession for Brahmanand Swami and where Khaiyo Khatri lived.

entities.name: Mangrol
entities.description: A town where Jhinabhai went and learned about Kamalshi Vanjha's illness.

entities.name: Mount Govardhan
entities.description: A mountain that Shri Krishna Bhagwan propped up with one finger, used as comparison to Maharaj's divine power.

entities.name: Muli
entities.description: The location where Brahmanand Swami was instructed to build a mandir and where he eventually resided and passed away.

entities.name: Muli mandir
entities.description: The temple where Devanand Swami became mahant after Brahmanand Swami, completing its construction and increasing its prosperity.

entities.name: Mumbai
entities.description: A city where Nirgun Swami helped Satsang grow through inspirational letters and visits. He was brought here for treatment during his illness.

entities.name: Mumbai mandir
entities.description: Temple in Mumbai where Jetha Bhagat served as kothari.

entities.name: Munibawa's ashram
entities.description: The ashram in Surat where Brahmanand Swami studied Sanskrit under Munibawa.

entities.name: Nadiad
entities.description: The original birthplace of Jagannath (Shukanand Swami) before his family settled in Dabhan.

entities.name: Nagher
entities.description: The region where Panchala village is located in Sorath, the southern part of Saurashtra.

entities.name: Neem Tree
entities.description: The tree under which Maharaj was seated in assembly at Dada Khachar's darbar when he announced the coming of a mukta from Dabhan.

entities.name: palace
entities.description: The nawab's palace in Junagadh where Maharaj and his sadhus were ceremoniously received.

entities.name: Panchala
entities.description: City where Ramanand Swami held court and where Jhinabhai lived. Site of grand festivals and the famous Fuldol celebration of 1823.

entities.name: Pen
entities.description: A village a short distance from Mumbai where Nirgun Swami was taken for treatment during his illness.

entities.name: Pij
entities.description: Village near Nadiad where Jethabhai was born and where Shastri Yogeshwardas and Sadguru Jagatpavandas would visit.

entities.name: Pij mandir
entities.description: The temple in Pij where Bhagatji Maharaj appeared and granted darshan to Jethabhai.

entities.name: Pij mandir
entities.description: Temple in Pij where Bhagatji Maharaj first appeared before Jethabhai, granting him darshan.

entities.name: Piplad
entities.description: A place with a well where Maharaj stopped to bathe after visiting the Khodiyar Mata mandir.

entities.name: pradakshina area
entities.description: The area behind the mandir where circumambulation takes place, where Yagnapurushdasji and Jethabhai were talking.

entities.name: Pune
entities.description: A distant city mentioned by Joban as the extent of his former banditry activities, from Vartal all the way to Pune.

entities.name: Purushottampura
entities.description: A place about three kilometers from Radhu where Ashabhai owned a farm and lived, where his house was destroyed by fire.

entities.name: Radha Vav
entities.description: A step well on the outskirts of Gadhada where Maharaj went to meet the incoming mukta from Dabhan.

entities.name: Radhu
entities.description: A place where Ashabhai bought land with Swamishri's guidance and where a month-long parayan was organized.

entities.name: Rajasthan
entities.description: The region where Brahmanand Swami's family returned after accepting his decision to become a sadhu.

entities.name: Rajkot
entities.description: City where Yagnapurushdasji was studying.

entities.name: Ramanandi mandir
entities.description: A temple in Sadhi village that was managed by brothers Ashabhai and Ishwarbhai.

entities.name: river bank
entities.description: The location where Devanand Swami's body was taken for his final rites to be performed.

entities.name: River Ghela
entities.description: The river where sadhus would bathe in the morning as part of their daily rituals.

entities.name: River Malan
entities.description: River in Mahuva where Jethabhai would accompany Bhagatji Maharaj for bathing.

entities.name: Royal Court of Junagadh
entities.description: The court where darbars gathered with entertainment, alcohol, and where Jhinabhai sat aloof from worldly pleasures.

entities.name: Royal Court of Shirohi
entities.description: The court hall where young Ladudanji performed his poetic recital before the Maharaja and captivated the audience.

entities.name: Royal Court of Shirohi
entities.description: The royal court where young Ladudanji first performed his poetry and gained recognition.

entities.name: Sadhi
entities.description: A village near Vadodara where brothers Ashabhai and Ishwarbhai lived and managed a Ramanandi mandir.

entities.name: Sankaleshwar Mahadev
entities.description: A small, beautiful mandir dedicated to Bhagwan Shiv located on the outskirts of Balol and Dhingda villages.

entities.name: Sarangpur
entities.description: Location of a mandir under construction that received support from Ashabhai and Ishwarbhai.

entities.name: Sarangpur mandir
entities.description: A temple where murti-pratishtha was fast approaching and for which money was needed for murtis from Jaipur.

entities.name: Saurashtra
entities.description: A region in Gujarat where Sorath (the southern part) is located, which contains Panchala village.

entities.name: Sayajipura
entities.description: Location of Ashabhai's farm where a grand festival was held instead of the simple ponk feast originally planned.

entities.name: Shahibaug
entities.description: The area in Ahmedabad where Swaminarayan Aksharpith publisher is located.

entities.name: Shirohi
entities.description: A region in present-day Rajasthan where Brahmanand Swami was born and where the royal court was located.

entities.name: Shvetdvip
entities.description: One of the divine abodes offered by Maharaj to Jhinabhai as a destination after death.

entities.name: Sorath
entities.description: A region in Gujarat where Bhagwan Swaminarayan came after traveling across India.

entities.name: Sorath Region
entities.description: A geographical area for whose devotees Jhinabhai requested that a mandir be built in Junagadh.

entities.name: stable
entities.description: The place where Maharaj's horse rested, covered by thick growth of a banyan tree, where Joban attempted the theft.

entities.name: Surat
entities.description: A city where Brahmanand Swami went to study Sanskrit in Munibawa's ashram and where Maharaj was later invited.

entities.name: Umreth
entities.description: A place from where the yogi (Nilkanth Varni) came to Vartal.

entities.name: Unmatt Ganga
entities.description: Another name for the River Ghela where Bhagwan Swaminarayan met Jivuba.

entities.name: Vadhwan
entities.description: Location of a mandir where Akshar-Purushottam murtis were installed with Ashabhai's help in preparations.

entities.name: Vadhwan mandir
entities.description: A temple where Akshar-Purushottam murtis were installed with preparations assisted by Ashabhai.

entities.name: Vadodara
entities.description: A kingdom that Maharaj mentioned as one of the worldly offerings he could give Jhinabhai, before offering the superior Akshardham.

entities.name: Vadodara mandir
entities.description: The temple in Vadodara where Jethabhai met Shastri Yagnapurushdasji and came daily.

entities.name: Vaikunth
entities.description: One of the divine abodes offered by Maharaj to Jhinabhai as a destination after death.

entities.name: Vartal
entities.description: A village where Maharaj celebrated Holi festival at Joban's request and where a mandir was built. Joban's home was located here.

entities.name: Vartal mandir
entities.description: A temple in Vartal for which Maharaj performed the groundbreaking ceremony in April 1822 and which Joban helped construct.

entities.name: Vaso
entities.description: A village where Joban Pagi visited and where Kashiyabhai lived, who was amazed at Joban's transformation.
